question:
Two days after vaginal delivery of a healthy newborn at term, a 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 2, is unable to breastfeed. Her labor was complicated by antepartum hemorrhage and she received two units of packed red blood cells. Her pulse is 99/min and blood pressure is 90/55 mm Hg. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show which of the following sets of serum findings?
 $$$ ACTH %%% Aldosterone %%% Cortisol $$$?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Antepartum hemorrhage -> blood loss -> decreased blood volume -> activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system -> increased aldosterone -> retention of sodium and water -> increased blood pressure -> 90%
enhanced_information: Antepartum hemorrhage can lead to decreased blood volume, activating the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system. This results in increased aldosterone levels, leading to sodium and water retention, and ultimately increased blood pressure. The correct set of serum findings is likely to be increased aldosterone (↑), normal cortisol (normal), and increased blood pressure (↑).
analysis: Antepartum hemorrhage can lead to decreased blood volume, activating the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system. This results in increased aldosterone levels, leading to sodium and water retention, and ultimately increased blood pressure. Given the patient's presentation with low blood pressure and inability to breastfeed post-delivery, the most likely set of serum findings would be increased aldosterone (↑), normal cortisol (normal), and increased blood pressure (↑).
